children: U.S. equities turned lower Thursday as investors weighed new wholesale-price data and a jump in government bond yields.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJI) was down about 0.6%, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite each slipped around 0.5%.
Only two of the S&P 500's 11 sectors were advancing, with consumer staples among the gainers and materials under pressure.

Data showed producer prices rose 0.4% in August from July, matching the expected increase. July's reading was revised to a 0.1% gain from zero previously reported. Weekly initial jobless claims also came in with a smaller-than-expected decline.

Bond markets reacted with higher yields. The two-year Treasury yield added nine basis points to 4.53%, while the 10-year yield reached 4.91% after rising seven basis points. The 30-year yield increased five basis points to 5.34%.
Investors were also following escalating Middle East tensions after U.S. Central Command said American forces destroyed five Iranian crude tankers.
Separately, crude prices remained above $100 a barrel, adding to concerns about inflation and the path for interest rates.

title: Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq Dips as Yields Jump After PPI Report
